topic: Why Nathu La in Sikkim is stranger than you think
hook: Your permit to Sikkim's border pass puts you metres from Chinese soldiers, and only Indians can go.
title: Why Nathu La Is Stranger Than You Think
description:
Nathu La in Sikkim is a high Himalayan pass where Indian and Chinese soldiers stand on either side of a wire fence. In this video we go through seven true facts about it: Sikkim's days as a kingdom, the old Silk Road route, the years it was shut, who is allowed to visit, and the soldier people still talk about.

Subscribe for more places and facts that sound fake but are true.

#NathuLa #Sikkim #IndiaChinaBorder
comment_prompt: Would you visit Nathu La? Yes or no?

scenes.narration: Your permit to Sikkim's border pass puts you metres from Chinese soldiers, and only Indians can go.
scenes.headline: CHINA, METRES AWAY

scenes.narration: That is Nathu La, a mountain gap above four thousand metres, where two armies stand on either side of one wire fence.
scenes.headline: Nathu La Pass

scenes.narration: You will learn why this pass stayed shut for decades, and why soldiers honour a man who died in 1968.
scenes.headline: Shut for decades

scenes.narration: We start in Sikkim, a place that was not even part of India until 1975.
scenes.headline: Not India until 1975

scenes.narration: The biggest surprise is saved for last, because it is the fence itself. Stay till the end.
scenes.headline: The fence is last

scenes.narration: Seven facts, each one stranger than the last. We begin at the bottom of the mountain.
scenes.headline: Seven strange facts

scenes.narration: Fact one. Sikkim was a separate Himalayan kingdom, ruled by a king called the Chogyal.
scenes.headline: A Himalayan kingdom

scenes.narration: The Chogyal's family ruled for centuries, and Gangtok was its capital, the same city tourists start from today.
scenes.headline: Gangtok was the capital

scenes.narration: Even after India became independent in 1947, Sikkim did not simply become an Indian state.
scenes.headline: Not a state in 1947

scenes.narration: India protected it and handled its defence, but Sikkim kept its own king and its own flag.
scenes.headline: Own king, own flag

scenes.narration: Then in 1975, the people of Sikkim voted, and the kingdom became a state of India.
scenes.headline: The 1975 vote

scenes.narration: So the road to Nathu La runs through a land that was a kingdom within living memory.
scenes.headline: A kingdom, recently

scenes.narration: Sikkim is tiny, yet it touches three other countries: China, Nepal and Bhutan.
scenes.headline: Touches 3 countries

scenes.narration: It is also home to Kangchenjunga, the third highest mountain on Earth, visible from Gangtok on a clear day.
scenes.headline: Kangchenjunga

scenes.narration: And in 2016, Sikkim became India's first fully organic state, a fact most visitors never hear.
scenes.headline: India's first organic state

scenes.narration: But that old doorway between India and Tibet is exactly what makes our next fact so strange.
scenes.headline: A doorway to Tibet

scenes.narration: Fact two. Nathu La sits on an old branch of the Silk Road, linking Tibet with India.
scenes.headline: A Silk Road branch

scenes.narration: For centuries, traders walked this track with mules, carrying wool, silk and other goods over the mountains.
scenes.headline: Mules and wool

scenes.narration: On the way up, you pass Tsomgo Lake, a high mountain lake that freezes over in winter.
scenes.headline: Tsomgo Lake

scenes.narration: Prayer flags line the roadside, fluttering in the cold wind as the bends get sharper.
scenes.headline: Prayer flags

scenes.narration: The pass itself is above four thousand metres, higher than Darjeeling or Shimla.
scenes.headline: Above 4,000 metres

scenes.narration: At this height the air holds noticeably less oxygen, so tourists often get headaches and breathe hard on arrival.
scenes.headline: Thin air

scenes.narration: Even climbing a short flight of stairs can leave you gasping for breath.
scenes.headline: Stairs feel hard

scenes.narration: Snow often covers the road for long stretches, and soldiers must stay posted here through the winter.
scenes.headline: Snow-covered road

scenes.narration: And this pass was not always open. For many years, nobody could cross it at all.
scenes.headline: Once sealed

scenes.narration: Fact three. After the 1962 war between India and China, Nathu La was closed to trade.
scenes.headline: Closed after 1962

scenes.narration: The old route that had carried goods for generations simply went quiet.
scenes.headline: The route went quiet

scenes.narration: The border stayed sealed for more than forty years, and the mountain track sat empty.
scenes.headline: Sealed 40+ years

scenes.narration: For people on both sides, that meant a trade link of generations was cut.
scenes.headline: A link cut

scenes.narration: It finally reopened in 2006, with trade between India and China through the pass again.
scenes.headline: Reopened in 2006

scenes.narration: But do not imagine a busy market. Trade here is limited to certain goods and certain days.
scenes.headline: Limited trade

scenes.narration: Traders cross only at set times, and only with the right paperwork.
scenes.headline: Set times only

scenes.narration: So the pass that once carried Silk Road caravans now handles a small, tightly controlled trickle.
scenes.headline: A small trickle

scenes.narration: Next comes a rule that surprises many visitors, because not everyone is allowed to see this border.
scenes.headline: Not everyone can go

scenes.narration: Fact four. Nathu La is open to tourists, but only Indian citizens may visit.
scenes.headline: Indians only

scenes.narration: Foreign passport holders are not allowed up, and reports say that includes OCI card holders.
scenes.headline: Foreigners not allowed

scenes.narration: Indian visitors need a special permit, which you arrange through the tourism office in Gangtok.
scenes.headline: Permit from Gangtok

scenes.narration: Army posts line the road, and your permit is checked before you are allowed to go higher.
scenes.headline: Army checks on the way

scenes.narration: Visits are limited to certain days of the week, so check with Sikkim tourism before you plan.
scenes.headline: Only some days

scenes.narration: Carry a photo ID and warm clothes, and be patient, because the checks take time.
scenes.headline: Bring ID, warm clothes

scenes.narration: The result is odd: a live border where families come on holiday and take selfies.
scenes.headline: Selfies at a border

scenes.narration: If you like strange places and facts that sound fake but are true, subscribe, because there is more like this coming.
scenes.headline: Strange but true

scenes.narration: Now fact five shows how tense things once got up here.
scenes.headline: It got tense

scenes.narration: Fact five. In 1967, Indian and Chinese troops fought each other right here at Nathu La.
scenes.headline: Fighting in 1967

scenes.narration: It was one of the rare clashes between the two armies, and it happened on this narrow pass.
scenes.headline: A rare clash

scenes.narration: The two sides also faced a standoff in 2017 at Doklam, a plateau not far from Nathu La.
scenes.headline: Doklam, 2017

scenes.narration: Yet today, the same border has something no one would expect from soldiers who once fought.
scenes.headline: A surprise today

scenes.narration: On some national days, officers from both armies meet at the border and exchange sweets.
scenes.headline: Sweets at the border

scenes.narration: So the same few metres of ground have seen gunfire in one era and mithai in another.
scenes.headline: Gunfire, then mithai

scenes.narration: That does not mean the border is relaxed. Both sides keep soldiers posted all year.
scenes.headline: Still guarded

scenes.narration: Think about that contrast the next time you hear the word border.
scenes.headline: Think about that

scenes.narration: Next is a soldier whose story is told on this mountain, even though he died decades ago.
scenes.headline: A soldier's story

scenes.narration: Fact six. Near Nathu La, there is a shrine to Baba Harbhajan Singh, an Indian soldier.
scenes.headline: Baba Harbhajan Singh

scenes.narration: Accounts say he died in 1968 after falling into a fast stream while leading a mule train.
scenes.headline: Died in 1968

scenes.narration: Soldiers believe his spirit never left, and that he still warns them of danger in their dreams.
scenes.headline: A spirit that warns

scenes.narration: Whatever you believe, the shrine is real, and soldiers and visitors both stop there to pay respect.
scenes.headline: The shrine is real

scenes.narration: Faith or folklore, it shows how lonely and hard life on a high border can be.
scenes.headline: Life on a high border

scenes.narration: Many Nathu La trips include a stop at his shrine, so you can see this for yourself.
scenes.headline: A stop on the trip

scenes.narration: Now for the last fact, the one I promised at the start.
scenes.headline: The last fact

scenes.narration: Fact seven. At the top, the border is a simple wire fence.
scenes.headline: Just a wire fence

scenes.narration: On one side stand Indian soldiers. On the other side, just metres away, stand Chinese soldiers.
scenes.headline: Soldiers face to face

scenes.narration: You can stand on the Indian side and watch them watching you.
scenes.headline: They watch you too

scenes.narration: There is no giant concrete wall, no huge gate, just a fence, a line and a few uniforms.
scenes.headline: A fence and a line

scenes.narration: Nathu La is one of the few border passes where India and China have allowed trade across.
scenes.headline: One of few passes

scenes.narration: Together, India and China are home to billions of people, and here the line between them is a wire.
scenes.headline: Billions, one wire

scenes.narration: In winter, temperatures at this height fall below freezing, and soldiers stand there in thick jackets.
scenes.headline: Freezing guard duty

scenes.narration: The pass is also a pilgrim route. Indian pilgrims heading to Kailash Mansarovar travel over it into Tibet.
scenes.headline: A pilgrim route

scenes.narration: In 2017, after the Doklam standoff, China did not allow pilgrims through Nathu La, and the route reopened in 2018.
scenes.headline: Closed 2017, open 2018

scenes.narration: So this gate between two giant countries opens and closes with politics, not weather.
scenes.headline: Politics, not weather

scenes.narration: Let us go back to where we began: your permit, a vehicle from Gangtok, and a short walk uphill.
scenes.headline: Back to the start

scenes.narration: At the top is a fence, and on the other side stand Chinese soldiers, close enough that you can see their faces.
scenes.headline: Close enough to see faces

scenes.narration: A kingdom, a Silk Road track, forty years shut, and now a live border you can visit.
scenes.headline: Kingdom to live border

scenes.narration: Your permit, a wire fence, and Chinese soldiers just metres away. That is Nathu La.
scenes.headline: That is Nathu La

scenes.narration: Next in this series: the neighbour whose clocks run fifteen minutes ahead of India.
scenes.headline: Next: a strange clock
